pages.answer: Lovable Pro is the faster route to a polished full-stack web app: it generates React interfaces and provisions a Supabase backend (database, auth, storage) in one click, and is listed on AI Tools Zone at PKR 1,600 for 1 month. Bolt.new Pro runs a complete Node.js environment in your browser via WebContainers — terminal, npm packages and multiple frameworks — and is listed at PKR 5,600 for 1 month. sections: Prompt-to-app polish vs a full development environment in the browser

Lovable is opinionated: describe the app in plain language and it generates a production-style React, Vite and Tailwind CSS interface (with shadcn/ui components), then wires the backend for you. Bolt.new, built by StackBlitz on WebContainer technology, runs a complete Node.js environment inside the browser tab — you get a real terminal, npm installs, development servers and framework choice (Next.js, Vite, Remix, SvelteKit, Astro). Choose Lovable when the goal is a finished-looking client app quickly; choose Bolt.new when the project needs custom packages, non-React frameworks or backend code you control directly.
Credits vs tokens: how each platform meters AI work

Lovable charges credits per message: in Default Mode the cost varies with task complexity (a small style change can cost half a credit; adding authentication costs more), and Plan Mode is 1 credit per message. Pro includes 100 monthly credits plus 5 daily build credits. Bolt.new meters in tokens instead: Pro starts at 10 million tokens per month with no daily cap, and unused tokens roll over to the next month. The practical difference for freelancers is predictability — Lovable's per-message pricing is easier to quote against a client job, while Bolt's token pool rewards developers who batch work and watch consumption during long error-correction loops, which can burn tokens quickly.
Backends, databases and deployment

Lovable's backend path is Supabase, provisioned in one click: PostgreSQL tables, user authentication and storage buckets are created for you, and projects sync two ways with GitHub so you can export the code and host it anywhere. Bolt.new gives broader choice — its own database features, a choice of database provider on Pro, and native Supabase integration when you want it — but setup is more manual. Bolt deploys in one click to Netlify and pushes to GitHub; Lovable deploys to custom domains from inside the platform. If a project needs MongoDB, Redis or a custom microservice later, expect post-export work on Lovable; Bolt's container makes that experimentation easier from day one.
Workflow fit for Pakistani freelancers and agencies

For Upwork and Fiverr freelancers shipping client MVPs and SaaS prototypes against deadlines, Lovable's automated database wiring and polished default styling shorten the path from prompt to handover, and the exported React code lands in the client's own GitHub repository. pages.description: No international card? Compare the three working routes in Pakistan: a fintech Visa/Mastercard used correctly, app-store billing, or paying a local seller in PKR via JazzCash, Easypaisa or Raast.
pages.answer: You do not need a credit card to buy AI subscriptions in Pakistan. The working routes are: pay the vendor with an internationally enabled debit card (a Visa or Mastercard, not a mono-badge PayPak card), pay through an app store, or pay a local seller in PKR via JazzCash, Easypaisa, SadaPay, NayaPay or bank transfer (IBFT/Raast) and have the subscription arranged for you. AI Tools Zone sells its listed subscriptions for PKR payment on WhatsApp, with prices from PKR 450 a month.
sections: Why most Pakistani cards fail on AI websites

Most declines are not about credit cards at all. A mono-badge PayPak card is Pakistan's domestic scheme and cannot pay an international merchant at all. A Visa or Mastercard debit card fails when its international or e-commerce session is not activated, when the balance has no buffer for the bank's conversion fee and the Section 236Y advance tax deducted on top of the charge, or when the purchase would breach the State Bank limit of USD 30,000 a year in card-based cross-border spending, counted across all of a person's cards (FE Circular No. 07 of 2022). The step-by-step troubleshooting for each cause is in our guide to [paying for ChatGPT Plus in Pakistan](/blog/how-to-pay-for-chatgpt-plus-pakistan/).
Route 1: a fintech debit card, used correctly

You do not need a bank credit card to pay a vendor directly. Fintech accounts such as SadaPay and NayaPay issue internationally enabled Visa or Mastercard debit cards that can pay foreign merchants once the international session is active and the balance covers the charge plus fees and tax. The same applies to an internationally enabled debit card from a conventional bank. This route keeps the account entirely in your own name at the official dollar price: ChatGPT Plus and Claude Pro are $20 a month (about PKR 5,530 at the State Bank rate of PKR 276.52 per dollar on 19 November 2026, before your bank's markup and the 236Y advance tax). Our [JazzCash and Easypaisa guide](/blog/jazzcash-easypaisa-ai-tools-pakistan/) covers the fintech card route in more detail.
Route 2: app-store billing

Subscribing inside the official iOS or Android app moves billing to Apple or Google, which accept a wider range of local payment methods than the vendor's own web checkout. Prices inside apps can differ from web prices and the subscription is managed in the store, so compare before you commit. This route suits buyers who want the account in their own name but cannot get any card to work on the web checkout.
Route 3: pay a local seller in PKR

A local seller removes the card from the transaction entirely. On AI Tools Zone you choose a listed plan, confirm the exact offer on WhatsApp, and pay in PKR by JazzCash, Easypaisa, SadaPay or NayaPay, or by bank transfer (IBFT/Raast); the subscription is then provisioned as a private account or an upgrade on your own email. Listed prices include ChatGPT Plus at PKR 2,300 a month, Claude Pro at PKR 2,200 a month, Cursor AI Pro at PKR 2,800 a month and Runway at PKR 3,500 a month, with plans starting at PKR 450 a month — see the full list on the [pricing page](/pricing/). Delivery depends on the product: many plans arrive in 15 to 30 minutes, some take 30 to 60 minutes, and a few take 1 to 2 hours; the estimate is shown on each product page. The complete ordering walkthrough is in the master guide to [buy AI tools in Pakistan](/buy-ai-tools-in-pakistan/).
What Section 236Y actually taxes

Section 236Y of the Income Tax Ordinance is an advance withholding tax that banks collect on card payments abroad: 0.5% for people on the Active Taxpayers List and 1% for non-filers, per the FBR withholding tax rates card updated to 30 June 2026. It applies to the foreign card payment, so it is one reason a direct dollar subscription costs more than the headline price once bank markup is added. When you pay a Pakistani seller in PKR instead, your payment is a domestic payment, so no 236Y is deducted from it. Guides quoting 10% or 16% for 236Y are using invented figures — the current rates are 0.5% and 1%.
Before you pay anyone: safety checks

Whichever route you choose, confirm the exact plan, duration, access type and total PKR price in writing before sending money, and keep the chat. Prefer private access or an upgrade on your own email over shared logins — shared accounts expose your work and break when passwords change, as our guide to [private vs shared access](/guides/private-vs-shared-access/) explains. Replacement cover differs by listing: 31 of the 32 listings on AI Tools Zone include a 7-day or 30-day replacement warranty, and Gemini Pro is the one listing with none, so check the product page before ordering. Our [guide to choosing a seller](/blog/where-to-buy-ai-tools-pakistan/) lists the common scams and the verification steps to run first.

Why was my debit card declined on an AI website?

The usual causes are a mono-badge PayPak card, which cannot pay international merchants at all; an international or e-commerce session that is not switched on; a balance with no room for the bank's conversion fee and the Section 236Y advance tax (0.5% for filers on the Active Taxpayers List, 1% for non-filers) charged on top; or the State Bank's USD 30,000 annual limit on card-based cross-border spending. Our payment guide walks through checking each one.
Do SadaPay and NayaPay cards work for AI subscriptions?

Yes — SadaPay and NayaPay issue internationally enabled Visa or Mastercard debit cards, and they can pay foreign AI merchants when the international session is active and the balance covers the charge plus bank fees and tax. You can also use either account to pay a local seller in PKR via Raast or IBFT, which avoids the card route entirely.
What is the FBR Section 236Y tax on foreign AI subscriptions?

Section 236Y is an advance withholding tax banks deduct on card payments abroad: 0.5% for people on the Active Taxpayers List and 1% for non-filers (FBR withholding tax rates card, updated to 30 June 2026). It is charged on foreign card payments, not on domestic PKR payments, so paying a Pakistani seller in rupees carries no 236Y deduction on your payment.
